analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/gemma-pipeline-speed.md, lines 1-5) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines ~1085-1094) plus a date bump on line 3. No executable code, keys, attestation, wire protocol, or authorization logic is touched in the supplied evidence.

The docs describe a behavioral change in the source PR: Gemma 4 serial-prefill pipeline pairs now default to four concurrent lanes (`DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes`). Each lane is charged its full request state on every rank and admitted against live memory (`QwenResidentRuntime.reserveLane`). A lane that does not fit is refused alone. The changelog also says expert blocks are computed in a shared dispatch with unchanged arithmetic, and that the planner prior counts 8 of 128 experts.

The claims are consistent with the existing memory model: per-request live-memory admission remains authoritative, the activation floor still applies, and no load-time allocation is added. Relevant threat-model items are TB-007 and T-029 (resource exhaustion and availability) and T-010 (cancellation). The accepted prefix-cache risk T-041 is not affected by the supplied text.

The actual code is not in this batch, so I could not verify the following claims.
- The shared expert dispatch produces identical per-token bytes, with no cross-request data mixing in batch-decode rows. Row isolation across lanes (A-001 confidentiality between requests) is something the next pass should check if the code is supplied.
- Per-lane memory admission is enforced on both ranks.
- A cancellation or failure in one lane does not leak or stall the other lanes.
- The planner's hardware prior reduction (8 of 128 experts) cannot cause over-admission. It is described as a prior only, with live admission still applying.

No security regression is identifiable from documentation alone, and the threat model needs no update from these text changes.
